conviction_note: The H1 FY27 numbers (Jul-Sep quarter) are new and not pre-released, and the FY27 guide (8.5m Prime, EUR115m Cash EBITDA) is most likely reiterated. That puts the size at about 7%, given 54% 60-day realised volatility and Sep-1's -16% on a beat. The evidence on direction is balanced: Q1 beat consensus and is on track for the net-add target, the disclosed short fell from ~9% in June to 3.15%, there is an active buyback and Booking's European Q3 was strong; against that, the headline profit will be down sharply y/y and Sep-1 sold exactly that setup. So p_up is 51 and the scaled number is ~0, while the findings sum to +0.7. That gap is small positives that do not outweigh a reaction history that sells profit-down-but-on-plan prints.

session_check: bmo. This rests on the issuer's own practice, not a timestamp for this release: the 1Q FY27 invitation says results are 'released before market opens', available from 08:30 CET, webcast 13:00 CET (https://s202.q4cdn.com/903232390/files/doc_financials/2027/q1/Invite_1QFY27-Results_1st_Sep_2026.pdf), and H1 FY26 came out the same way on Tue 2025-11-18. I could not read the H1 FY27 invitation: the IR site sits behind a Cloudflare challenge and the guessed q4cdn filenames return 404. The date itself comes from the vendor calendar. Quartr lists 2026-11-13, but the 2026-11-13 tape (222k shares, -2%) does not look like a results day next to Sep-1's 2.49m shares, and a Tuesday fits the cadence. So I treat the event as real but not confirmed by the issuer.
positioning_check: The CNMV's per-issuer short page answered from this container even though the baseline grid did not: https://www.cnmv.es/portal/consultas/ee/posicionescortas?nif=A02850956 (read 2026-11-16). Disclosed net shorts above 0.5% are Citadel Advisors 1.46% (2026-11-02; flat at 1.47-1.50% since mid-September), Capital Fund Management 0.89% (2026-10-30; trimming from 1.28% on 2026-06-08) and ActusRay 0.80% (2026-11-06; up from 0.70% on 2026-09-18). That is 3.15% disclosed, against about 9% across about ten funds in early June (Merca2, 2026-06-04). The crowded short has largely covered; what remains is flat to slightly building into the print (ActusRay). Positions below 0.5% are not visible.

findings.finding: The disclosed net short has de-crowded from about 9% of capital in June (the most-shorted Mercado Continuo name) to 3.15% across three holders. CFM is trimming and Citadel is flat, while ActusRay added to 0.80% on 2026-11-06. The squeeze fuel that drove the +37% five-session move in June is mostly gone, but about 3% disclosed remains to cover on a good print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In June 2026, short covering after the FY26 beat took the stock +37% in five sessions (Merca2). On Sep-1 the stock fell -16% with the shorts still near 3-4%.
findings.original_quote: Citadel Advisors LLC | 1,460 | 02/11/2026; Capital Fund Management SA | 0,890 | 30/10/2026; ActusRayPartners Limited | 0,800 | 06/11/2026 (titular de la posición | % sobre el capital | fecha de la posición = holder | % of capital | position date); Merca2: 'una decena de hedge funds que mantenían posiciones cortas' ... 'cerca del 9% del capital' (about ten hedge funds held short positions, close to 9% of capital)
findings.why_not_priced: The baseline sealed positioning as unreadable, so no lean in this stage reflects it. If the market were treating EDR as crowded, the June squeeze pattern would be in the setup, and it is not: the shorts are a third of their June size.

findings.finding: EUR62.0m of buy-back is still committed to September 2027 (about 11% of market cap at 30 June), plus a further 9m-share amortisation, so the company is a steady bid into and after the print.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The buy-back did not prevent -16% on Sep-1 or -41% in Nov-2025.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced, having been public since September. It is filed because it is a mechanical one-day support that the run-up does not capture, and it is sized small for that reason.

findings.finding: H1 headlines will show profit and Cash EBITDA sharply down y/y. Q1 was net income EUR0.2m against EUR13.6m and Cash EBITDA -41%, with acquisition spend 'concentrated in our peak seasonal booking window', against H1 FY26's EUR94.0m Cash EBITDA and EUR31.5m net income. The Spanish press framed Q1 exactly that way and the stock fell 16% that day despite the beat.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Sep-1-2026: -16.4% on a quarter stated ahead of consensus with the guide reiterated. Nov-2025: -41% on the H1 print plus a Cash EBITDA guide cut.
findings.original_quote: Rankia forum reply titled with the news headline 'EDreams reduce su beneficio en su primer trimestre fiscal hasta los 200.000 euros por el aumento de costes' (eDreams cuts its Q1 profit to EUR200,000 on higher costs), and 'ver caer el EBITDA Cash un 41% no es fácil de digerir para el mercado' (seeing Cash EBITDA fall 41% is not easy for the market to digest)
findings.why_not_priced: The decline is inside the company's guided investment phase, so the market has been told to expect it, which is why this is sized near zero. It is filed because the local retail press reads the y/y headline, and on Sep-1 that reaction overrode the beat.

findings.finding: Booking Holdings' Q3 2026 (reported 2026-11-03) showed European room nights up high single digits and flight tickets up 19%, a healthy European demand read-through for eDreams' Jul-Sep quarter; EDR rose 6.3% on Nov-4 on 737k shares. Booking guided Q4 room nights to only +1-3%, citing Middle East disruption, higher airfares and reduced capacity.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov-4-2026: +6.3% on the read-through (Yahoo tape), which has since faded to 4.95 from 5.18.
findings.why_not_priced: It is largely priced. The Nov-4 jump and the fade since show the market traded it; what remains is Booking's Q4 caution, which cuts against eDreams' H2 commentary. I net the two to a small positive.
findings.independence: Ryanair H1 FY27 also flags Q3 fares modestly ahead but a closer-in booking window: https://www.travelextra.ie/?p=157802

findings.finding: Air-content access is still a drag. Q1 Cash Revenue Margin fell 2%, partly from 'intermittent air content access', and Ryanair, which is not an approved-OTA partner of eDreams, keeps campaigning against eDreams Prime (August 2026 OTA survey) while signing other OTAs.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None isolated; the dispute has run since 2023 without a dated price reaction to the content line.
findings.why_not_priced: It is mostly priced as a long-running dispute. It is filed because it is the one line in the Q1 deck that the company did not attribute to planned investment.

findings.finding: The FY27 guide is on track. Q1 net adds of 173k are 29% of the 600k target in 25% of the year, Q1 profitability beat sell-side consensus, and management calls the guide built on 'conservative, high-certainty foundations' and says it has met both previous 3-year plans. That favours a reiteration or a modest beat over a cut on the line that moves this stock most.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Nov-2025 guide cut: -41%. Feb-2026 9M beat with the guide reaffirmed: +20.6%. May-2026 FY beat and FY27 guide: +37% over five sessions. Sep-2026 Q1 beat with the guide reiterated: -16%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced: the stock is still below its pre-Q1 5.56 at 4.95 and 60 days down 8.7%, which is consistent with the market discounting delivery risk on the FY27 guide that the Q1 data do not support. A market that believed the guide would not show a -16% Q1 day that never recovered.

baseline_tension: The findings lean slightly positive, against a flat lean (-0.15, the 20-day run-up of +2.9% on a 60-day -8.7%). They are mostly orthogonal to the run-up (positioning, buy-back, guide pace), and the reaction history (Sep-1 -16% on a beat) argues against trusting the positive lean, which keeps p_up at 51.
language_note: The CNMV per-issuer short-position page (Spanish, 'posicionescortas?nif=A02850956', and the per-holder 'posicionescortascomunicaciones' histories) gave the dated positioning the baseline marked unreadable: 3.15% disclosed, against Merca2's (Spanish) ~9% in June. No English source carried either number.

The Spanish press and the Rankia retail forum carried the y/y headline framing of Q1 ('reduce su beneficio ... hasta los 200.000 euros'), which is the reaction mechanism behind Sep-1's -16%; the English wire copy led with 'ahead of consensus'.
The Spanish sources added nothing on consensus, the H1 date or any pre-release.
lessons_applied: The 'finding inside what the company already guided' rule (via the core table) moved the y/y profit-decline finding from -0.5 to -0.3, because the decline lands inside the guided investment phase.

'Positioning covered:false is not a zero' / 'a crowded short is fuel': I reported the CNMV per-issuer page that did read, and kept the positioning finding at +0.3 because the short has de-crowded rather than built; no size change.

'The move is in the guide' (reiterated 2.3% vs new numbers 7.4%): I kept abs_move_pct at 7.0 rather than cutting it toward 2.3, because the numbers are new and this name's last two prints with a reiterated guide moved -16% and +21%; no change.
'Reaction history vetoes direction, not size': nudged p_up from 50 to 51 only, to reflect the small positive findings sum, without letting the Sep-1 sell-off shrink abs_move.
